question: Is the integer-repair status-4 failure caused by SciPy >= 1.17 rejecting the forwarded HiGHS 'threads' option, as ARCHITECTURE.md and IMPROVEMENT_PLAN research correction 1 state?
answer: No, on two counts. (1) The trigger is ORDER, not the option: when threads=1 is the first HiGHS solve in a process it succeeds and so does every later solve; when a default-thread solve runs first, every later threads=1 solve returns status 4 '(HiGHS Status 0: Not Set)' for the life of that process. This matches the documented HiGHS global scheduler, whose thread count is fixed by the first solve; a fork pool inherits it from the parent. (2) The boundary is 1.15, not 1.17.
consequence_for_the_pin: The declared range 'scipy>=1.11,<1.17' ADMITS 1.15.x and 1.16.x, both of which reproduce the failure. A fresh 'pip install -r requirements.txt' today resolves to scipy 1.16.x and hits it. Measured in this session: tests/test_pfe.py passes 128/128 when the threads test runs alone but fails 38 tests when the whole file runs, all with 'joint integer projection was not resolved by the solver' — the fail-closed path firing correctly on a solver that was refused a thread-count change. RECOMMENDED, not applied here: narrow the bound to <1.15 in requirements.txt, .github/workflows/ci.yml and tests/test_pfe.py::test_solver_compatibility_range_is_pinned_in_ci_and_requirements. Left to A2/the maintainer because it narrows everyone's environment and the repository has an active review loop on exactly this file.
limitations: Two-variable synthetic model, not the production integer-repair problem.
Single process; no fork pool exercised.
Linux/CPython 3.11.15 only; the original deadlock was observed on macOS.
Patch versions only as resolved by pip on this date; not every release tested.
Does not test whether threads=1 is still needed once the start method or solve ordering changes — that is work package A3 candidate 0.

runs.conclusion: order-dependent: the first HiGHS solve fixes the process thread count
